kitDescription: Kurumi is an Iron AR Supporter whose kit revolves around inflicting a named 'Hacked' status on the boss. Every 36 normal attacks she hacks her target, and she also hacks all enemies whenever she uses her own Burst Skill; each hack deals 52.24% of her final ATK as sustained damage every second for 5 seconds. While the boss is Hacked and the team is in Full Burst, every further 36 normal attacks trigger an extra hit of 86.17% of final ATK on the target. Her Burst Skill itself deals no damage — it makes all enemies take 18.06% more damage for 10 seconds, amplifying the whole team's output. In practice she is a Burst-I debuffer whose personal damage comes from the repeating Hacked damage-over-time and the Full-Burst rider it enables.

redAssertions: Failure A — NON-VACUITY probe ('expected 0 to be greater than 0'): blind helper wired onEvent at the top level of the runComp argument instead of inside cfg, so its event log was empty; independent probe of the SAME fixture with cfg.onEvent wiring finds 6 damageTakenPct buffApply + 6 kurumi burstCast events. Blind-test artifact (RECON_ERROR), not an override defect.

Failure B — 'teammates byte-identical under damage counterfactuals' (~0.04% diff): blind fixture controlComp('kurumi') seats TWO Burst-I units (liter + kurumi); DoT ticks feed burst gauge (skillGauge on the dot-tick path), so zeroing kurumi's DoT shifts B1 slot contention and perturbs liter/crown/helm burst timing by ~0.04%. A faithful engine interaction violating the blind byte-identity assumption (RECON_ERROR), not an override defect.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA exists: all four kit lines are FAITHFUL, cross-corroborated by the prose, the formula SSOT, and both blind agents. The two S5 reds are blind-test artifacts, not divergences — one is a harness miswiring (top-level onEvent never delivered events; a correctly-wired probe of the same fixture shows 6 debuff applications on 6 kurumi casts), the other is a broken byte-identity assumption (DoT ticks feed burst gauge, so in the blind's two-B1 fixture zeroing the DoT legitimately perturbs liter's burst timing by 0.04%); both are RECON_ERROR with hard evidence supplied. The 13 green S5 assertions independently re-derived every load-bearing encoding (hitCount:36, burstCast-not-fullBurstEnter, fbGate+requiresTargetStatus 'Hacked', damageTakenPct 18.06/10s on the boss), and S6's override is byte-identical except an explicit crit:true that matches the engine default — and because the driver is Qwen while both blinds are claude, this agreement is cross-family, stronger than the usual same-model convergence. Discrimination holds on every load-bearing test, with the one masked case (requiresTargetStatus gate removal is inert in the driver fixture because burstCast keeps Hacked up through most FB windows) documented and re-routed through status-application removal, which cleanly zeroes S2. What must change for GO: nothing. Owner spot-check residuals (all documented ⚑s, none blocking): (1) Hacked re-application is shipped as stacking independent DoT instances — if the real status REFRESHES, S1 damage is overcredited during overlap windows (both blinds and the driver share this engine-native reading, so it is the one place agreement proves nothing); (2) the 5s Hacked status window is inferred from the DoT duration, kit-silent; (3) S2's 36-hit counter is read cumulative-with-gate rather than per-FB-resetting. A Hacked popup/footage read settles all three when available.
